crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin holds near $64K as traders eye Hormuz and jobs data
crypto-macro.summary: Crypto edged higher with BTC around $64,000 and ETH near $1,880, buoyed by hopes of a Hormuz reopening and Friday's jobs report.
body: Bitcoin traded near $64,038, up about 1% on the day, while Ethereum opened around $1,868 and firmed to roughly $1,881 in early trading. The total crypto market rose about 0.7% to a capitalisation near $2.27 trillion on $52.2 billion of volume.
Traders pointed to Trump's comments that a Strait of Hormuz reopening could come within days and to Friday's July jobs report as the near-term catalysts most likely to shift risk appetite.

crypto-macro.h3: Fear index ticks up but sentiment stays cautious
crypto-macro.summary: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index rose to 27, still in Fear territory, off the prior day's Extreme Fear reading.
body: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index stood at 27, in Fear territory but improved from 25 (Extreme Fear) a day earlier, reflecting slightly steadier sentiment as prices firmed.
The cautious tone underscores how macro risk, from oil to rates, continues to dominate crypto positioning.

crypto-macro.h3: BlackRock sets 1-for-3 reverse split on its Ethereum ETF
crypto-macro.summary: BlackRock announced a reverse split for ETHA aimed at lowering trading costs.
body: BlackRock announced a 1-for-3 reverse split for its spot Ethereum ETF, ticker ETHA, a move it said would help lower trading costs for investors.
The change is a housekeeping step that leaves underlying exposure unchanged while adjusting the share price and count.

crypto-macro.h3: Solana governance clears first vote to double disinflation rate
crypto-macro.summary: A proposal to accelerate Solana's token issuance reduction passed an initial governance vote.
body: Solana's proposal to double its disinflation rate cleared an initial governance vote, advancing a change that would speed the reduction of new token issuance over time.
Supporters frame it as tightening SOL's long-run supply schedule, while the measure still faces further governance steps.

crypto-macro.h3: Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% as it waits on the labor market
crypto-macro.summary: The FOMC kept rates steady at its July meeting, with unemployment at 4.2% and inflation still above target.
body: The Federal Reserve held the federal funds target range at 3.50% to 3.75% at its July 29 meeting, judging the labor market consistent with maximum employment while inflation remained above its 2% goal. Unemployment stood at 4.2%.
Markets are watching August payrolls closely: further deceleration could revive rate-cut expectations and ease elevated yields, whereas resilient hiring keeps the Fed on hold.

crypto-macro.h3: Stocks rally as Hormuz hopes lift risk appetite
crypto-macro.summary: US equities jumped, with the S&P 500 up 1.79% and the Nasdaq up 2.59%, on optimism over the strait and softer rate fears.
body: US stocks rallied, with the S&P 500 climbing 1.79% to 7,736.52, the Nasdaq gaining 2.59% to 26,584.99 and the Dow adding 907 points, or 1.71%, to 54,085.88, as investors welcomed signs of a possible Hormuz de-escalation.
The move extended a recovery from late July, when a softer jobs backdrop had put Fed rate cuts back in focus.

crypto-macro.h3: Gold holds firm awaiting a Hormuz outcome
crypto-macro.summary: Bullion traded in a holding pattern as investors weighed the odds of a strait reopening against lingering geopolitical risk.
body: Gold prices held steady as traders awaited clarity on the Strait of Hormuz, balancing hopes of a deal that would ease supply fears against the risk of renewed escalation.
The metal's resilience reflects continued demand for safe havens even as equities and crypto rallied on de-escalation optimism.

crypto-macro.h3: Cysic token surges as niche launches draw flows
crypto-macro.summary: Amid a steadier tape, the Cysic token jumped sharply, a reminder of speculative pockets in altcoins.
body: The Cysic token soared about 93% in a session, highlighting how speculative flows persist in smaller-cap tokens even as majors trade cautiously.
Such moves underscore the divergence between blue-chip crypto sentiment, still in Fear, and episodic frenzies in newer listings.

crypto-macro.h3: Analysts split on what a steady Fed means for BTC
crypto-macro.summary: With the Fed on hold, forecasters reach sharply different conclusions on Bitcoin's next move.
body: Commentators drew four different conclusions from the same Fed hold, ranging from constructive to cautious for Bitcoin, reflecting deep uncertainty about the path of rates and liquidity.
The spread of views captures a market caught between dovish hopes tied to a softening labor market and the drag of still-elevated real yields.

mental-health.h3: APA survey: most psychologists now hear about AI in therapy
mental-health.summary: More than three-quarters of psychologists say patients discuss AI in sessions, and over a third have patients using chatbots as an additional source of support.
body: A 2026 American Psychological Association survey found more than three-quarters of psychologists report patients discussing AI in therapy, and over a third say patients are turning to AI as an additional mental health resource, for support, self-diagnosis or even companionship.

Only about a quarter of psychologists thought patients would one day prefer chatbots to human clinicians, suggesting confidence that the therapeutic relationship offers benefits AI cannot yet replicate.

mental-health.h3: Reviews: human therapists still beat chatbots on severe cases
mental-health.summary: The 2026 evidence shows humans outperform AI for moderate-to-severe anxiety and depression, and chatbots miss crisis signals.
body: A review of the 2026 research finds that every study comparing chatbots with human therapists for moderate-to-severe anxiety or depression shows human clinicians produce significantly better outcomes. Critically, AI chatbots cannot reliably detect suicidal ideation or psychiatric emergencies.
The findings temper enthusiasm for AI as a standalone treatment while leaving room for supportive, clearly-bounded roles.

mental-health.h3: JAMA Pediatrics tracks teen chatbot use for mental health
mental-health.summary: New research examines how US adolescents and young adults use, and disclose, AI chatbots for mental health.
body: A JAMA Pediatrics study looked at AI chatbot use and disclosure for mental health among US adolescents and young adults, adding data on how younger users engage with these tools and whether they tell anyone.
The work feeds a growing evidence base that clinicians and regulators are using to shape guidance for youth-facing AI.

mental-health.h3: NEJM AI reports randomized trial of a generative chatbot
mental-health.summary: A randomized trial published in NEJM AI tested a generative AI chatbot for mental health treatment.
body: NEJM AI published a randomized trial of a generative AI chatbot for mental health treatment, one of the more rigorous evaluations of a large-language-model tool in a controlled setting.
Randomized designs like this are helping move the field beyond observational claims toward measurable clinical effect.

mental-health.h3: FDA weighs a framework for generative AI mental health devices
mental-health.summary: Following a late-2025 advisory meeting, the FDA is building rules for generative-AI-enabled mental health software.
body: The FDA is developing its regulatory approach to generative-AI-enabled digital mental health devices after a November 2025 Digital Health Advisory Committee meeting on the topic. Apps that claim to diagnose, guide treatment or serve as prescription interventions generally need clearance as Software as a Medical Device.
There are now more than 1,300 FDA-authorised AI-enabled medical devices, with mental health among the fastest-growing segments.

mental-health.h3: FDA-CMS TEMPO pilot aims to speed digital health to patients
mental-health.summary: A joint pilot seeks to bring certain digital health devices to Medicare and Medicaid patients while safeguarding safety.
body: The FDA launched the TEMPO pilot with CMS to help bring certain digital health devices, including some mental health tools, to Medicare and Medicaid patients while protecting safety.
The effort reflects growing attention to reimbursement pathways, long a barrier to adoption of digital therapeutics.

mental-health.h3: Lived-experience study centers safety in chatbot design
mental-health.summary: People with depression describe wanting actionable help, bounded emotional validation and personalization without unsafe data disclosure.
body: A JMIR Mental Health qualitative study centred on people with lived experience of depression found they judge AI chatbots by intertwined priorities: actionable information, emotional validation with clear limits, and personalization that does not require unsafe disclosure of sensitive data.
The insights offer designers concrete guidance on building tools that feel supportive without overpromising or mishandling private information.

mental-health.h3: Acceptance of AI therapy varies across patients and clinicians
mental-health.summary: New work compares willingness to use AI mental health interventions among clinicians, patients and the public.
body: A study examined acceptance of AI for mental health interventions among clinicians, patients and the general community, finding differing levels of comfort across groups and use cases.
Understanding these gaps matters for deployment, since tools that clinicians distrust or patients resist will struggle regardless of technical performance.
